claim.pdf_says: Page 760 ends with 'Format 9 (program-pointer-assignment):' followed by the single syntax line 'SET { identifier-7 } ... TO  identifier-8'. Nothing further is printed on page 760. Page 761 then OPENS with its own first line, the label 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):', above the Format 10 syntax diagram 'SET  { identifier-9 } ... { UP / DOWN } BY arithmetic-expression-3'.
claim.markdown_says: ISO_COBOL.md line 30846 (inside the page-760 slice, immediately before the anchor): 'SET { identifier-7 } ... TO identifier-8 Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):' -- and the page-761 slice then jumps straight into the fenced Format 10 diagram with NO label of its own.
claim.why_it_matters: The Format 10 label has been welded onto the end of the Format 9 syntax skeleton. Read literally, the Format 9 general format now appears to contain the trailing tokens 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):', which is not COBOL syntax and corrupts a general-format line; simultaneously the Format 10 diagram is left orphaned with no format label, so a reader (or a generator walking the page anchors) cannot tell which SET format the UP/DOWN BY diagram belongs to. Format 9 and Format 10 are distinct SET formats with different syntax rules and general rules.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted to refute on all five grounds and could not; both sources were checked independently at 300 dpi and by exact grep. (1) PDF SIDE CONFIRMED. Rendered E:/Temp/specrecon/v760/spec_p760.png (PDF page 760 = printed page 730). Reading down the page: Format 4 (condition-setting) + diagram, Format 5 (object-reference-assignment) + diagram, Format 6 (attribute) + diagram, Format 7 (data-pointer-assignment) + diagram, 'Format 8 (function-pointer-assignment):' + 'SET { identifier-12 } ... TO identifier-13', then 'Format 9 (program-pointer-assignment):' + 'SET { identifier-7 } ... TO identifier-8'. Below that syntax line the page is BLANK for roughly the bottom quarter, down to the footer '730  (C)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license line. The string 'Format 10' appears nowhere on page 760. (2) PDF page 761 (printed 731) rendered separately: its FIRST printed content line, directly under the running head 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', is 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):', with the diagram 'SET { identifier-9 } ... { UP / DOWN } BY arithmetic-expression-3' beneath it. So in the PDF the label unambiguously belongs to page 761 and is a separate display line, separated from the Format 9 skeleton by a large vertical gap, a page footer, a page break, and a running head. (3) MARKDOWN SIDE CONFIRMED VERBATIM. grep gives exactly one hit: line 30846 = 'SET { identifier-7 } ... TO identifier-8 Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):'. The page-761 anchor is at line 30848, so 30846 sits inside the page-760 slice, exactly as claimed. The page-761 slice is: anchor, '## Page 761', '**ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)**', two blank lines, then straight into the fenced Format 10 diagram -- no format label of its own. Claim quotes both sources accurately; no misquotation. (4) NOT PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE. The misplaced token is not a running head, footer, page number, or license line -- it is a substantive normative label that names one of the fourteen distinct SET general formats. Furniture rules do not apply. (5) NOT LINE WRAPPING OR REFLOW. The two texts are separated in the PDF by ~25% of a page of whitespace plus the footer plus the page boundary plus the next page's running head; nothing about that is a soft wrap. (6) NOT MISSING-TEXT-PRESENT-ELSEWHERE. The harm here is not omission but merger: the label is present, on the wrong side of the page boundary AND fused into a general-format line. (7) MEANING DOES CHANGE. Formats 8, 9 and 13 are the only SET syntax skeletons in this run that are NOT inside fenced code blocks in the transcription -- they are bare paragraph text. That is the mechanism that permitted the fusion, and it is also why the damage is semantic rather than cosmetic: a reader or tool consuming line 30846 as the Format 9 general format sees the trailing tokens 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):' as part of the syntax skeleton, which is not COBOL and not in the standard. Conversely a generator slicing content between the page-760 and page-761 anchors gets an unlabeled UP/DOWN BY diagram. Format 9 (program-pointer-assignment, SET ... TO) and Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic, SET ... UP/DOWN BY) carry different syntax rules and different general rules, so conflating or orphaning them is materially wrong. CONFIRMED REAL.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is accurate as written; verified against the 300 dpi renders of both PDF pages and against the markdown by exact grep. Three refinements for the fix record. (a) Page mapping: PDF page 760 is printed page 730 and PDF page 761 is printed page 731, so the label crosses a real printed-page boundary, not just a slice boundary. (b) Partial mitigation, which does not defeat the finding: the transcription's editorial figure-notes line at ISO_COBOL.md:30858 does read 'Figure notes (SET statement Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic) syntax diagram)', so a human reader can still recover which format the orphaned diagram belongs to. But that annotation is transcriber-added apparatus, not the standard's own printed label, and it sits AFTER the diagram; the normative label line printed at the top of page 761 remains absent from the page-761 slice, and the Format 9 general-format line on page 760 remains corrupted regardless. (c) Root cause and scope of the fix: the Format 9 syntax skeleton at line 30846 is bare paragraph text, unlike Formats 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 14 in the same SET run, which are all inside ``` fences. Formats 8 (line 30842) and 13 (line 30887) are unfenced in the same way. The correct repair is to move 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):' to be the first content line of the page-761 slice, immediately above its fenced diagram, and to fence the Formats 8, 9 and 13 skeletons so the same fusion cannot recur -- rather than merely splitting line 30846 in place, which would leave the label on the wrong page.
